name: MITRE ATT&CK
description: Adversary tactics, techniques, subtechniques and defensive mitigation mappings for WinSec Analyzer.

references.title: Encrypt Sensitive Information
references.description: MITRE ATT&CK M1041 describes encryption of sensitive information, including full-disk encryption. This is defensive context, not a detected attack technique, proof of an incident or a complete mitigation test. Encryption does not prevent all access by an adversary in an already unlocked session.
references.recommendation: Review sensitive-data exposure and the threat model for stored data. Have the authorized administrator address confirmed encryption or protection deviations under approved policy with verified recovery arrangements. Review access controls separately; do not infer compromise or complete attack prevention from a BitLocker state.

references.title: Disable or Modify Tools
references.description: Adversaries can interfere with defensive tools. A disabled protection alone does not prove an attack, malicious intent or this technique occurring.
references.recommendation: Establish whether the disabled protection was authorized, review relevant security records, and have the authorized administrator restore the approved protections. Repeat the WinSec read-only assessment; investigate suspected tampering through the normal incident response process.

references.title: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
references.description: Vulnerable signed drivers can support privilege escalation. A missing ASR setting is a local configuration deviation, not evidence that exploitation occurred; this rule does not prevent loading existing vulnerable drivers.
references.recommendation: Review exposure to vulnerable drivers and approved execution protections. Have the authorized administrator configure this specific ASR rule, assess driver allow/block policy separately and review relevant events if exploitation is suspected. Repeat a read-only assessment.

references.title: Update Software
references.description: M1051 contextualizes software maintenance as a defensive measure. Disabled automation is not evidence of an attack or a complete mitigation test.
references.recommendation: Have the administrator restore approved update automation after resolving the confirmed deviation. Verify deployment separately; review application, driver and firmware maintenance outside this OS check.

references.title: Update Software
references.description: A missing cumulative Windows baseline informs software maintenance. It does not identify an exploited vulnerability, detected technique or compromised device.
references.recommendation: Have the administrator review the confirmed baseline gap and complete approved patch deployment with compatibility and restart checks. Investigate suspected exploitation separately; WinSec performs no remediation.

references.title: Update Software
references.description: A release without reviewed vendor security support requires maintenance planning. This lifecycle observation neither detects an attack nor proves complete protection.
references.recommendation: Plan migration to a supported Windows release with the administrator, including compatibility and recovery checks. Review remaining software maintenance separately; the original lifecycle result remains unchanged.

references.title: Filter Network Traffic
references.description: Host Firewall configuration contributes context to network filtering. Disabled profiles, permissive defaults and broad exceptions require review. Logging is complementary monitoring context. These observations do not prove compliance, reachability, exploitation or complete mitigation.
references.recommendation: Review the effective policy for Domain, Private and Public profiles, approved application and service exceptions, block precedence, and monitoring requirements. Have an authorized administrator apply the approved filtering policy; reassess through a confirmed read-only scan.
